In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the conformational change induced by the reduction of the disulfide bond in thioredoxins is a localized event involving the two half-cystine and two tryptophans residues.

reduction of the disulfide bond of E. coli thioredoxin causes a conformational change of the protein which is reflected in the chemical shift of the proton of Trp-28 but not in the chemical shift or the line shape of the proton of the other tryptophan, Trp-31.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the PMR data indicate that the conformational changes of E. coli thiodeoxin are localized in the region around the disulfide bond.

the PMR studies in Hz0 indicate that the conformational changes of the two tryptic fragments of oxidized thioredoxin are different upon reduction and that the two tryptic peptides of thioredoxins from E. coli and yeast have different conformations in the oxidized and reduced states.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the PMR spectra of reduced and oxidized E. coli thioredxin are very similar in H20 at pH values above 6.0.
the conformation of the reduced form of thiodeoxin is more stable than that of the oxidized protein at pH values below the isoelectric pH.
the redox-induced conformational change of thioredoxins is not limited to the vicinity of the redox active cysteines.
